_: THE WORKED-EXAMPLE ATLAS. A finite library of deliberately designed composition templates, each with rigid horizontal structure and a small number of prescribed responsive states. Generalisability comes from CHOOSING THE RIGHT TEMPLATE, not from letting the browser invent a composition. This replaces the composition resolver, which is retained as research evidence only (docs/mockups/compositions/) and whose layout-selection logic must not be ported into the app.
hierarchy: 1  page family          Worked examples                                     author / lesson generator
2  pedagogical pattern  single · sequence · comparison · visual check        author / lesson generator
3  composition template one of the six below, named in the JSON             explicit
4  content slots        prompt, steps, answer, visual, interpretation, …    JSON content
5  responsive state     wide / narrow                                       the template
_  THE GOVERNING RULE: layer 5 may rearrange a template. It may never choose a different template.

invariants.identity: A template's identity is authored and never inferred. No measurement — occupancy, relative height, remaining width, preferred figure scale — may turn one template into another. The atlas build asserts that `data-tpl` is character-identical at every width and for every adversarial payload.
invariants.height: Ordinary Study pages are `height:auto` and may grow without limit. The page scrolls. Nothing is shrunk, compressed or recomposed to avoid vertical scrolling, and page height is not an optimisation target.
invariants.horizontalRigid: Horizontal relationships are rigid and belong to the template. Vertical dimensions are fluid and belong to the content.
invariants.measure: Every prose region has a controlled measure, so a stacked example does not expand text across the whole canvas. Unused page width is reading margin and is correct.
invariants.figures: A figure is sized from its own mathematical and legibility requirements. Surrounding prose never determines a figure's width. The only automatic classification permitted is MEDIA GEOMETRY — portrait · balanced · landscape · wide — which is a design input a template maps to an approved subdesign.

measures._: These are design-system values. They never appear in lesson JSON.

figureClasses._: Media geometry, from the authored domain's aspect (height ÷ width at equal unit scale). A class is a DESIGN INPUT, not a size.

single.flow.wide: one column at the flow measure: title · QUESTION · rule · WORKED SOLUTION · ANSWER · synthesis
single.flow.narrow: identical — only the measure stops clamping. THERE IS NO STATE CHANGE.
single.flow.note: The overwhelmingly common shape, and the default. A seven-step solution simply becomes taller.

single.split.pattern: one worked example whose prompt carries substantial information
single.split.wide: SCENARIO / QUESTION | rule | WORKED SOLUTION · ANSWER
single.split.note: Authored, never inferred. A short prompt in this template stays split — that is the author's decision, and the atlas proves it with an adversarial payload.

sequence.flow.wide: repeat(single.flow), a hairline between, synthesis after the whole sequence
sequence.flow.note: The count is irrelevant: two, three, five or ten items are the same repeated child.

comparison.paired.wide: CASE A | CASE B, then WHY THEY AGREE at the synthesis measure
comparison.paired.narrow: case A · case B · why they agree
comparison.paired.note: Paired because the author said it is a comparison, not because the two happen to be the same height.

comparison.sharedVisual.pattern: two cases and the object that explains them

subdesigns.side: cases row, then SHARED VISUAL | INTERPRETATION — for a portrait or balanced figure
subdesigns.down: cases row, then the visual at full width, then WHY THE TWO AGREE beneath — for a landscape or wide figure

comparison.sharedVisual.chosenBy: the figure's media-geometry class, which is a property of the authored figure
comparison.sharedVisual.narrow: case A · case B · visual · interpretation

visualCheck.pattern: workings, then the same question read off the figure

states.2 Graph check: GRAPH | INTERPRETATION for a portrait or balanced figure; the graph at full width with the interpretation beneath for a landscape or wide figure

visualCheck.note: Two authored views of one example.

keptFromTheResolverResearch: figure intrinsic and legibility information — the measured ladder of sizes a plane can be drawn at
equal-unit safeguards — px per authored x-unit against px per y-unit, read off the painted SVG
overflow detection — an unsettable line scrolls locally
tests for unowned space inside an allocated region
discardedAsLayoutAuthority: optimisation or scoring across candidate arrangements
attempts to use all available space
the assumption that a page ought to avoid vertical scrolling
